notes: run.py builds a repo per run from `fixture`, runs `prompt` with `claude -p`, then applies the fixups with `git rebase -i --autosquash <base>` in a clone. grade.py applies `common_checks` plus each eval's `checks`. File checks read the clone after the rebase. Check types are in grade.py and ~/.config/ai/evals/harness.py. Regexes are case-insensitive unless a check sets `case`, except `reply_*` checks. `@name` in `patterns` names a list in `pattern_sets`.

No push, rebase, reset, stash, checkout, switch, merge, cherry-pick, or amend

evals.name: reply-pasted
evals.prompt:
/deslop reply

Great question! It's worth noting that the new cache layer genuinely leverages a robust LRU strategy — it serves as the backbone of the read path. Importantly, the cache holds at most 512 entries and evicts the least recently used entry first. Entries expire after 15 minutes. If you call `Cache.clear()`, all entries are removed immediately. See the [cache docs](https://example.com/docs/cache) for tuning options. In conclusion, this streamlines reads and delivers a seamless experience.
evals.expected_output: Only the new text: no slop, all facts, the link as `cache docs (https://example.com/docs/cache)`. No git, no file writes.
